attack.note: Cho is the melee half of Cho'gall. Basic attacks matter in the Seared Flesh, Frenzied Fists and Hammer of Twilight builds, and C'Thun's Gift at level 20 makes them ranged. The pair together is a ranged damage threat through Gall.

poke.note: Rune Bomb is a slow rolling skillshot detonated by Gall for 210, and Gall's Dread Orb and Shadow Bolt Volley add long range sustained poke. The guide calls Cho'gall a ranged bruiser that safely pokes several opponents.

damage.note: Sustained damage from Gall's Dread Orb plus Cho autos, with real burst from Twisting Nether and Upheaval combos. Uppercut adds percent health damage. Enraged Regeneration applies healing reduction through Dread Orb. Measured 2101 hero damage per minute and 4918 damage taken per minute, the highest damage taken of the group. Numbers may reflect only Cho's own body, not Gall's output.

good_into.why: Huge health pool, Consuming Blaze heals per enemy ignited, Enraged Regeneration and Surging Dash sustain, and Twilight Veil armor make him durable against chip damage.
Gall's Dread Orb, Shadow Bolt Volley and Twisting Nether reach the backline from a safe tank body, and Upheaval pulls them into the team.
Hammer of Twilight pushes and stuns, Power Surge slows, and Twilight Veil armor blocks autos while Cho'gall out damages melee heroes with Gall behind him.
Power Surge slow and Surging Fist catch low mobility heroes, and Favor of the Old Gods roots with Upheaval, which the guide ties to Twisting Nether.
Enemy teams with no healing cannot punish with attrition, and Cho'gall scales into the strongest late game in the game, per the guide.

bad_into.why: Cocoon or Containment Disc turns the fight into a 5v3 because both halves are locked, and Surging Fist and Upheaval can be interrupted.
Percent damage such as Cursed Bullet, Last Rites and Seven Sided Strike ignores armor, and a death costs two heroes worth of experience.
He occupies two slots, so the team has four bodies and loses map presence and rotation, and he is weak in the early game.
Cho's melee body is hard to get on a kiter without C'Thun's Gift, and Gall alone is stationary.
Snowball maps and early objectives punish his weak early game and the four man team, as the guide says on Battlefield of Eternity and Warhead Junction.

wants_from_team: A dedicated single target healer such as Alexstrasza, Brightwing or Ana
A resilient bruiser with waveclear to cover macro
A teammate to play Gall and talk, plus a team that can play with only four bodies
No second assassin so the team is not too fragile
gives_team: A huge health pool frontline with a second ranged damage source
Long range sustain poke from Gall
Displacement and stuns from Hammer of Twilight and Upheaval
weaknesses: Weak early game, snowball maps punish him
Two heroes die with one death
Percent damage and stacked crowd control
Draft is easily countered and uses two draft slots
evidence: Surging Fist, Consuming Blaze, Rune Bomb, Upheaval, Hammer of Twilight, Ogre Hide ability text
Talents Seared Flesh, Frenzied Fists, Twilight Veil, Molten Block, C'Thun's Gift, Enraged Regeneration, Hour of Twilight
Icy Veins: strongest late game in the game, best as the only assassin, requires a dedicated healer
measured: hero damage 2101 per minute, damage taken 4918, siege 3390, win rate 0.448 in 105 games
owner_notes: Cho and Gall are one hero in game played by two players. Cho is the bruiser half.

lens_notes.damage_delivery: Cho melee autos plus Gall Dread Orb and Shadow Bolt Volley. Owner read: Cho is the bruiser half of one hero played by two people.
lens_notes.damage_reach: Cho is melee, Gall reaches long range. Medium is the pair average.
lens_notes.kill_pattern: Hammer of Twilight, Upheaval and Twisting Nether chain. Heroic chains brute force kills.
lens_notes.escape: Surging Dash and Shove give an escape when low.
lens_notes.utility_tool: Twisting Nether silences, Enraged Regeneration applies healing reduction through Dread Orb.
lens_notes.camp_play: 3.5 camps per game measured, the highest of this group.
lens_notes.power_curve: Guide: strongest late game in the game and weak early. Measured win rate 0.448 in 105 games.
lens_notes.snowball: He does not snowball from early kills, he scales and can come back late.
lens_notes.execution_demand: Needs two players who talk, and a death costs two heroes.
lens_notes.durability_source: Measured damage taken 4918 per minute, the highest here, so the health pool is how he lives.

lens_gaps: no lens for a hero that takes two draft slots and two players, and costs two kills when it dies (Cho and Gall)
no value on team_needs for a team that must play with four bodies on the map
